booter-quirk:AvoidRuntimeDefrag: OCLP base: keeps Apple's EFI runtime services from being defragmented by boot.efi, so firmware NVRAM and time services keep working after the handoff
booter-quirk:EnableSafeModeSlide: OCLP base: lets the kernel slide be chosen in safe mode as in a normal boot
booter-quirk:EnableWriteUnprotector: OCLP base: lets OpenCore patch boot.efi and the kernel in memory on this firmware (CR0.WP off during the patch)
booter-quirk:FixupAppleEfiImages: OCLP base: loads Apple's legacy EFI images (this Mac's own firmware drivers) under OpenCore's W^X memory rules
booter-quirk:ProvideCustomSlide: OCLP base: picks a kernel slide that avoids the firmware's reserved memory on this Mac
booter-quirk:SetupVirtualMap: OCLP base: gives the firmware runtime services a virtual memory map, needed on this 2012 firmware
kernel-patch:Initialize early VM range b: hao kernel repair (kc-binder, kc.bind): the Darwin 27 kernel starts on Ivy Bridge; tests/test_kc_bind.py proves the bytes
kernel-patch:Pass early kernel-map reser: hao kernel repair (kc-binder, kc.bind): Darwin 27 early kernel-map bounds on this Mac; tests/test_kc_bind.py
kernel-patch:Preserve bootstrap physical: hao kernel repair (kc-binder, kc.bind): bootstrap physical-page aliases survive on Ivy Bridge; tests/test_kc_bind.py

kernel-patch:netrec: even boot progress: Recovery/NetBoot installer only (rec-progress-phase): an even progress bar while the installer boots; not in an installed image's config
kernel-quirk:AppleCpuPmCfgLock: OCLP base: this Mac's firmware locks MSR 0xE2 (CFG Lock); AppleIntelCPUPowerManagement would panic writing it
kernel-quirk:AppleXcpmCfgLock: OCLP base: the same CFG Lock workaround for the XCPM power-management path
kernel-quirk:DisableIoMapper: OCLP base: VT-d DMA remapping off (legacy Intel graphics and Wi-Fi drivers misbehave with it on this OS). Security: no IOMMU DMA protection; known, listed in SEC2 (P6)
kernel-quirk:DisableLinkeditJettison: OCLP (build.py, with Lilu): the kernel keeps __LINKEDIT so Lilu and its plug-ins can resolve symbols
kernel-quirk:PanicNoKextDump: OCLP base: a panic report stops after the backtrace instead of listing every kext (readable panic logs)
kernel-quirk:PowerTimeoutKernelPanic: OCLP base: a power-state change that times out (legacy audio and display drivers on an unsupported OS) does not panic
kernel-quirk:ProvideCurrentCpuInfo: OCLP base: gives the kernel this CPU's TSC and bus frequency, which newer kernels no longer derive for Ivy Bridge
kernel-quirk:ThirdPartyDrives: pipeline/targets/mbp92.json third_party_sata_ssd: TRIM for non-Apple SATA SSDs, the drives users fit when they upgrade this Mac (it shipped with an HDD or an Apple SSD); a profile assumption, not a measurement of one laptop

kext:AppleIntelCPUPowerManagement.kext: OCLP (firmware.py): Ivy Bridge CPU power management, removed from macOS 13; patched to attach whatever intel_cpupm_matching says

nvram:WriteFlash=True: OCLP base: OpenCore's NVRAM Add values persist in flash (Startup Disk and boot-args survive). Security: weakened values persist for other boot paths; known (SEC2 P6)
security:AllowSetDefault=True: OCLP base: Ctrl+Enter in the OpenCore picker sets the startup disk
security:ApECID=0: Apple Secure Boot ECID unused (SecureBootModel Disabled)
security:BlacklistAppleUpdate=True: OCLP base: Apple firmware update payloads are not run on this Mac (they are not for it under macOS 27)
security:DmgLoading=Any: OCLP base: OpenCore loads any DMG (the Recovery and the NetBoot images are not Apple-signed). Security: unsigned boot images load; known (SEC2 P6)
security:ExposeSensitiveData=15: OCLP base: OpenCore publishes its version, boot path and OEM info to the OS (OCLP's tools read it)
security:HaltLevel=2147483648: OpenCore halts only on its own fatal errors (DEBUG_ERROR)
security:ScanPolicy=0: OCLP base: the picker scans every device and file system (USB installers, NetBoot)
security:ScanPolicy=2049: the USB installer's picker: scans only what it boots from
security:SecureBootModel=Disabled: OCLP (security.py): Apple Secure Boot off, required for a modified kernel and System on this Mac. Security: no verified boot chain; known, user disclosure (SEC2)
security:Vault=Optional: OCLP base: OpenCore does not verify its own files (no vault). Security: EFI changes are not detected; known (SEC2 P6)
uefi-quirk:EnableVectorAcceleration: OCLP base: SSE-accelerated hashing in OpenCore (faster boot)
uefi-quirk:RequestBootVarRouting: OCLP base: macOS's Startup Disk writes go to OpenCore's own boot variables, so macOS cannot make the firmware skip OpenCore
